title: How Trajectory Length Degrades Monitor Detection

original_idea.body:
# How Trajectory Length Degrades Monitor Detection

**Problem:** SHADE-Arena notes that even frontier agents 'often miss critical details or reference their secret side task in long trajectories' — but the dual question, how monitor detection degrades as trajectories get longer, is the deployment-relevant one and is not isolated.

**Direction:** Take SHADE-Arena malign transcripts and create truncated/extended variants of controlled lengths. Have a fixed monitor score each length bucket and plot AUROC vs trajectory length. Determine whether long trajectories help the monitor (more evidence) or hurt it (signal diluted, attention limits).

**Why it matters:** Real agentic deployments run very long trajectories; if monitor reliability decays with length, audit budgets must scale accordingly. A clean experiment_variation on length using an existing benchmark, inference-only.

**Relevant context:** SHADE-Arena (arXiv 2506.15740): agents miss details and reference side tasks in long trajectories; top monitor AUC 0.87. Ensemble Monitoring (arXiv 2605.15377) on monitor calibration.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: monitor decay with trajectory length informs audit budgeting for long deployments.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Length-bucket transcripts, fixed monitor scoring; accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped AUROC-vs-length curve with clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Clean benchmark-based study labs skip, public data.

novelty.reasoning: Length effect noted for agents; monitor-side degradation may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Noted for agents; monitor side open.
